solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Body of work produced by company (American)

parts.note: CORP is the standard short form of corporation, a company
US, as in the United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: An author's output is described as the product of an American firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpus is the whole collection of writings or works by one author or on one subject.

clue.text: King is regularly sombre and not uplifted

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of sombre

indicators.note: in a down entry, something lifted up is read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: nor is a conjunction meaning and not

explanation.surface: A monarch is described as gloomy and in low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: OBERON is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the fairy king in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, so he is a king by literary example.

clue.text: Poor signs misinterpreted as indicator of things to come

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so the letters are taken in a wrong order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad omens read wrongly are taken as a forecast of what lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast, especially a doctor's forecast of how an illness will develop.

clue.text: TV programme thus introducing a poet and artist

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
taken as written
Alexander Pope, the 18th-century English poet
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A television show is said to present a poet alongside a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' places the word for thus in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on television or radio, so it is a type of TV programme.

clue.text: Remaining faithful is a horrible grind, eh?

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled and ugly, so the following letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that staying loyal is a dreadful slog.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere to a belief or rule is to stick to it loyally, so adhering means staying true.

clue.text: Emergence of a Republican challenger

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a rival is a competitor or challenger

explanation.surface: A new Republican contender steps onto the political scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is an appearance or coming into being, as in the arrival of a new idea, hence emergence.

clue.text: Type of accommodation all the rage with the Spanish

parts.note: hot means very fashionable, all the rage
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A kind of lodging is said to be hugely popular with Spaniards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is an establishment providing rooms and meals for travellers, one kind of lodging.

clue.text: Journey on horseback around grand hill- range

indicators.note: around says one word goes about another, enclosing it inside

parts.note: a ride is a journey on a horse
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone rides a horse round a large range of hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow stretch of high ground, a line of hills.

clue.text: Absence of bad material in good composing work

parts.note: no expresses the absence of something
tat is cheap, tasteless stuff
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A composition is praised for having no weak passages.
explanation.walkthrough: Tat is British slang for shoddy goods or junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Notating means writing music down in notation, which is the written side of composing.

clue.text: Elegant young socialite currently doing a radio show?

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young woman entering society
on air means broadcasting right now

explanation.surface: A stylish young society woman is presenting a radio programme at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a man who is confident, stylish and charming, so it means suave and elegant.

clue.text: Why people use Tinder up until now?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the reason for a dating app, in order to go on dates
second meaning: so far, as yet

explanation.walkthrough: Tinder is a dating app; the phrase is read once as purpose and once as a time expression.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as an infinitive of purpose for going on dates and as an adverb meaning so far.

clue.text: 2 travelling somewhere in Asia

indicators.note: travelling means moving around, so the letters move into a new arrangement

parts.note: the answer to clue 2, the fairy king

explanation.surface: The fairy king is on a journey to a place in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia shared by Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei.

clue.text: Personal attendant with time to take in Lima, a capital city

indicators.note: to take in means to admit or swallow, so a letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's personal servant
T is the abbreviation for time
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A manservant and a timepiece are taken to Lima, which is a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the capital city of the clue, but it only gives the letter L; the capital is in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Valletta is the capital of Malta, so it is an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Boy beginning to loathe going on a date

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of loathe
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A boy starts to hate the idea of going out on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a boy or young man.

clue.text: Creature close to death in nasty old pen, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement among many, so the letters are reordered
the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of death
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal near death is kept in a filthy old enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shetland pony is a small hardy breed of horse from the Shetland Isles, so it is a creature.

clue.text: Nobody's initially attending university gathering, of course

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word, so only its opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of nobody
at means present at, attending
U is the abbreviation for university
a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: Nobody turns up at a campus meeting, unsurprisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally and of course are both used to mean as might be expected, a direct synonym.

clue.text: 'Do some cocaine' is the policy of many politicians

parts.note: a do is a party
a line is a dose of cocaine laid out for sniffing

explanation.surface: Taking drugs is cheekily described as the shared habit of politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: The party line is the official stance a political party expects its members to follow.

clue.text: Entitled person of a certain sort primarily seen in pubs

indicators.note: in says these pieces sit inside the next word

parts.note: bars are pubs
one can mean a certain person, as in a one for the ladies

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter alone is taken

parts.note: the first letter of seen

explanation.surface: A titled lady of a particular kind is mainly spotted in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness holds a noble title, so she is a titled person; entitled is read as having a title.

clue.text: Bloke's amused reaction creates serious offence

parts.note: a bloke is a man; the apostrophe s stays
laughter is the reaction to amusement

explanation.surface: A man laughing causes deep offence to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is the crime of killing someone without intent, a grave criminal offence.

clue.text: Excellent, short printed works

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for great or exciting
second meaning: a shortening of literature, written works

explanation.walkthrough: 'short' belongs to the second meaning: the word is a clipped form of literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit is current slang for excellent and also the informal abbreviation of literature, printed writing.

clue.text: Animal's mistake crossing one river

indicators.note: crossing means stretching over and across, so one word spans the others

parts.note: a gaffe is an embarrassing blunder
I is the Roman numeral one
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An animal blunders while crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is an African mammal with a very long neck, an example of an animal.

clue.text: After a couple of days, was the manager flustered?

parts.note: taken as written
two Ds, D being the abbreviation for day
led means was in charge

explanation.surface: After two days in charge, the new boss appears rattled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the word for was the manager after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled and confused, close to flustered.

clue.text: Gossip about award that's not important

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: natter is idle chatter
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Chatter about a prize that hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Natter is British slang for chat.
explanation.definitionFit: No matter is said of something that is unimportant or does not count, as in it is no matter.

clue.text: Modify plug fitting

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: Someone changes the plug on an appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug fitting' reads like electrical work; a plug is also a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to alter something to suit new conditions, which is to modify it.

clue.text: Present, say, ultimately won't make even kids smile

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so each following word gives its final letter

parts.note: the final letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A gift, it seems, ends up failing to make even children smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but it is the grammatical present.
explanation.definitionFit: The present is one grammatical tense, alongside past and future, so it is an example signalled by say.

clue.text: City periodically rainy and periodically hot

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of rainy
the first and third letters of and
the first of the alternate letters of hot

explanation.surface: A city where the weather is now wet and now scorching.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of each word are taken; from hot only the first one is needed, a slight looseness.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Extremely reasonable, principal alternative to Brexit

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of reasonable
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: Staying in the EU is touted as the very sensible main alternative to leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK's 2016 referendum the choice was Leave or Remain in the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Remain was the referendum option to keep Britain in the EU, the opposite choice to Brexit.

clue.text: Weak story in which evil is overturned

indicators.note: in which says the following piece is set inside the story word

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so the word runs back to front

parts.note: ill means evil or harm

explanation.surface: A feeble tale in which wickedness is defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallible means liable to err, so having a weakness.

clue.text: Kind of oddly sweet air

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters fall into a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A melody that is sort of strangely sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' is a tune in the surface, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were and kind of both soften a statement, meaning in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Yen slide ruined financial returns

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the word is broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slump in the Japanese currency wrecks investment income.
explanation.definitionFit: Yields are the income produced by an investment, its financial returns.
